section13_checks.prohibition_description: Treating Grant Agreement Annex templates as the governing structural schema for proposal writing.
Inventing call constraints, scope requirements, expected outcomes, or expected impacts not present in Tier 2B.
Inventing project facts (partners, capabilities, roles, objectives, budget figures, team sizes, equipment) not present in Tier 3.
Commencing Phase 8 activity before the budget gate (Phase 7) has passed; asserting unvalidated budget figures.
Storing durable decisions only in agent memory without writing them to Tier 4.
Allowing a workflow or skill to become a de facto constitutional authority.
Silently reordering phases or weakening gate conditions to allow progress with incomplete inputs.
Finalizing proposal text when source state is incomplete/contradictory/unvalidated without flagging the gap.
Using agent-local knowledge of Horizon Europe rules as a substitute for reading Tier 1 documents.
Producing Tier 5 outputs not traceable to specific inputs in Tier 1-4.
Modifying Tier 1 or Tier 2 source documents to reflect project-specific assumptions.
Treating CLAUDE.md as advisory or optional.

check_reasoning.13.1: No structural reference to a Grant Agreement Annex, Model Grant Agreement Annex, or AGA template is used as a schema authority. References to 'Part A' are to the application form's Part A (Tier 2A), not to a grant agreement annex.
check_reasoning.13.2: The review packet references standard MSCA evaluation sub-criteria (1.1-1.4, 2.1-2.3, 3.1-3.2) and the 50% Excellence weighting solely as the review lens for assessing the drafted sections. It does not inject any new call requirement, scope boundary, or eligibility condition into deliverable content. The review_packet.v1 schema carries no traceability_footer by design (it is a QA artifact, not a claim-bearing proposal section); no invented call constraint is asserted.
check_reasoning.13.3: Applied conservatively. All project facts named (ELTE, Hollos, Jung, Krumatic, AgroVIR, DrR, deliverables D1.1-D2.2, WP structure, person-month figures, publication counts, Eurostat figures, 8-30% ranges) appear as quotations or paraphrases OF the excellence/impact/implementation sections under review (see per-finding 'evidence' fields carrying quoted text). The review packet is the auditor of these facts, not their fabrication origin; it introduces no project fact absent from the sections it reviews.
check_reasoning.13.4: The review packet contains no monetary budget figures (no EUR/euro amounts asserted as confirmed values). Person-month references (e.g. '9.0 PM', '30 PM total') appear as quoted effort figures inside review findings about workload feasibility in the reviewed implementation section, not as newly asserted confirmed budget values. Under the TAPM input boundary the phase7 budget_gate_assessment file was not re-read (verification of gate pass is the scheduler/gate-evaluator responsibility, not this artifact-level audit); no budget-dependent claim is originated by this artifact.
check_reasoning.13.5: Not verifiable from artifact content alone; enforced by the decision-log-update skill and Tier 4 write discipline.
check_reasoning.13.6: Not verifiable from an artifact; scope-expansion is a runtime/authority concern, not detectable in review packet content.
check_reasoning.13.7: The review packet is a Phase 8 artifact and references only Phase 8 sections (excellence, impact, implementation). It references no activity from a phase higher than its own phase context; no evidence of silent reordering.
check_reasoning.13.8: The review packet explicitly surfaces and flags incomplete/assumed source state (ELTE participation and co-supervision pending written confirmation, farmer-site field access to be secured, AgroVIR holds no PIC, host Part A verification outstanding). It performs the opposite of concealment, consistent with the flag-the-gap requirement of §13.8.
check_reasoning.13.9: No Horizon Europe regulatory rule (participation condition, grant agreement term, financial regulation) is asserted as fact from programme knowledge. Programme terms (PIC, beneficiary, associated partner, Part A) appear as review vocabulary describing project facts drawn from the reviewed sections, not as sourced regulatory claims.
check_reasoning.13.10: The review packet's content is derivative of and traceable to the reviewed Tier 5 sections, each finding citing a specific section and quoting supporting evidence; it introduces no untraceable new claim. The review_packet.v1 schema does not define a traceability_footer / no_unsupported_claims_declaration field, consistent with its QA-artifact nature; the specific field-level mechanism of this check is therefore non-applicable, and the substantive traceability requirement is satisfied.
check_reasoning.13.11: Not checkable from a deliverable artifact; no Tier 1/Tier 2 source document is written or modified by a review packet.
check_reasoning.13.12: Not directly checkable from an artifact; the review packet operates within, and does not override, the constitution.
